study_name.notes: No canonical study name provided in the paper; study is referred to by condition investigated (anorexia nervosa).

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

country.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2; microbial DNAs were isolated using NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY‑NAGEL)
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction; Methods — DNA extraction, 16S rRNA sequencing
dna_extraction_kit.notes: NucleoSpin is a Macherey-Nagel product; mapped to NorgenBiotek category as closest match in allowed_values for soil-type DNA extraction.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: Primary sequencing for metagenomic analysis; 16S rRNA in mouse experiments used IlluminaMiSeq.

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases

sex.evidence_quote: Since 90–95% of individuals with diagnosed AN are females, we decided to include only women

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

subject_id.notes: Individual subject identifiers are not provided in the paper; only cohort-level and sample-level aggregates reported.

sample_id.notes: Individual sample identifiers are not provided; cohort totals reported (n=77 AN, n=70 HC faecal samples).

age.notes: Age reported as 'age-matched' but specific per-sample ages not disclosed in main text or supplementary tables provided.

age_group.notes: Age group categories not specified; participants appear to include adolescents and adults based on inclusion in EDI-3 (ages 13–53 years) but granular classification not provided.

control.notes: Paper distinguishes AN cases (n=77) vs. healthy controls HC (n=70) at cohort level but does not assign case/control labels to individual samples in the data provided.

ncbi_accession.notes: No NCBI SRA/ENA accessions provided in the main text or supplementary materials.

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not discussed in this study.

age_min.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_min.notes: This is the lower age bound of the EDI-3 questionnaire age range, not explicitly stated as the cohort minimum age.

age_max.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_max.notes: This is the upper age bound of the EDI-3 questionnaire age range, not explicitly stated as the cohort maximum age.

age_years.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN (females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr) and three HC (females aged 20, 22 and 21 yr)
age_years.notes: Mean ages calculated from FMT donor groups. Human cohort ages not explicitly stated as aggregate; only FMT donors ages provided.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Participants were excluded if they had received antibiotics within 3 months, ensuring no current antibiotic use at enrollment.

bmi.evidence_quote: women with AN were much leaner, had lower fasting serum concentrations of glucose and insulin
bmi.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
bmi.notes: AN cohort mean BMI ~11.5 (derived from Supplementary Table 1); HC mean ~21.6; specific subtype BMIs not aggregate reported. FMT donor BMIs explicitly stated in Methods.

dietary_restriction.notes: Dietary information not reported; acknowledged as study limitation: 'we had no information on diet and physical activity.'

disease.evidence_quote: AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria for the restricting or binge/purging subtypes of AN
disease.notes: Study comprises two main groups: AN cases (77 females) and healthy controls (70 females).

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: AN-RS: n=56; AN-BP: n=21 (as stated in Figure 1b caption).

disease_response_orr.notes: ORR not applicable; study focuses on mechanistic microbiota pathogenesis, not treatment response measurement.

disease_response_pfs.notes: PFS not applicable; eating disorder study, not oncology.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: PFS not applicable; eating disorder study.

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria not applicable; study is not a solid tumor response trial.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool phenotypes (consistency, color, frequency) not reported; only microbiota composition and metabolomics analyzed.

fmt_id.notes: No study-specific FMT participant identifiers provided in the paper.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: we transplanted faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free (GF) mice
fmt_role.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain and altered energy metabolism in mice
fmt_role.notes: Study involved FMT from human donors (AN-RS cases and HC) to germ-free mice recipients under energy-restricted feeding.

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed or reported.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Neonatal data not collected; study focuses on adult women with AN.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Delivery method data not collected; study focuses on adult women.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Neonatal feeding data not collected; study focuses on adult women with AN.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Gestational age not reported; study does not focus on neonatal outcomes.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Preterm status not reported; study involves adult women, not birth outcomes.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: The exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women were BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg m 21 −2 , regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills explicitly exempted from medication exclusion criteria for controls, indicating permitted use.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not reported; cohort appears primarily premenopausal based on age range (EDI-3 designed for 13-53 years).

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Pregnancy status not explicitly reported for enrolled participants.

smoker.evidence_quote: metadeconfoundR pipeline where covariates including age, BMI, smoking and multiple drug intake were corrected
smoker.notes: Smoking status was collected and used as a covariate in analyses but aggregate smoking prevalence/status not reported.

treatment.evidence_quote: All the included patients were treated in specialized centres. The species that were significantly different in abundance distribution between AN and HC after deconfounding interferences of multiple medications (selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines)
treatment.notes: Multiple medications documented. Both in-patients and out-patients enrolled in cognitive behavioural therapy courses and multidisciplinary care.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: AJCC tumor staging not applicable; study involves eating disorder, not solid tumor malignancy.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: TNM staging not applicable; eating disorder study, not oncology.

biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers identified in the study include bacterial species, metabolites, and functional modules.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Serum concentrations of both primary and secondary bile acids were higher in AN.
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type; most are reported as relative abundance or serum concentration.
